iterations.title: Baseline: one prompt to a frontier model with web search
iterations.decision: Reference point. Precision 79% (it flags little) but recall only 71%: it missed 4 of the 9 rules that directly change what a company must do, and it is the only setup failing trace checks (dates it could not verify, dates written into action text). This is what the pipeline has to beat.

iterations.title: Evals kick in: the first staged pipeline
iterations.decision: Kept as the starting point. Recall 98% vs the baseline's 71%, but precision only 45% — it fell for ~2.4 traps per run (look-alike rules, closed deadlines, paperwork notices). Next: make the filter stricter about what does NOT count.

iterations.title: A strict filter prompt that spells out what does not count
iterations.decision: Kept and promoted to the live user view (experiment.yaml → userView.setup). Precision 45% → 79.6%, trap hits 2.4 → 0.4 per run, recall 98% → 93%. Held up on the held-out test week (124/132 vs 109/132 cases right). Still 0.4 pts under the 80% precision target; next: find out what the remaining false flags and misses have in common (error analysis).

iterations.title: Fixes chosen by error analysis: every verified date on the card, indirect-supply rules, specific actions
iterations.decision: Rejected; live config stays on jev-sonnet-strict. Decided on dev weeks only: recall tied (27/27 both), precision fell 93.1% -> 79.4% (trap hits 2 -> 7). strict-v2's higher test-week recall (14/15 vs 9/15) is not used to choose, since picking a change because of the test week is overfitting. Kept: the every-verified-date card (dates right ~74% -> 100%) and the eval fixes (judges see shown dates, gist-level dev rubrics).

iterations.title: Steadier filter: run the LLM filter 3 times and keep what the majority says
iterations.decision: Rejected; live setup stays jev-sonnet-strict (the filterVotes knob stays in code, default 1). Rule: beat the winner on dev AND hold on test. Dev: recall tied 30/33, trap hits 5 -> 2, precision 65.2% -> 68.2%, filter flips between repeats 5 -> 1. Test does not hold: precision 73.3% -> 65.7% (trap hits 8 -> 12), and repeat agreement on test did not improve (flagged docs identical across all 3 repeats: 62% -> 64%; dev 72% -> 93%). Suite consistency metric 0.938 -> 0.944. Cost per run 2.2x ($0.126 -> $0.280). Judge pass 0.88 -> 0.82.

iterations.title: Fewer false alarms: don't flag rules that bind only the agency or only other kinds of entities
iterations.decision: Not promoted; no measurable effect. Live setup stays jev-sonnet-strict. Mechanism check on the targeted docs (flagged / runs that saw them, same suite): 2026-21964 strict 0/9 vs strict-v3 0/9; 2026-22865 0/9 vs 0/9; 2026-22743 2/9 vs 2/9. The control already left the first two alone in this suite (its hits on them in 04's suite, 1/9 and 2/9, were run-to-run noise), and the third is still flagged by both. Headline: dev recall 30/33 both, dev precision 88.2% -> 93.8% (trap hits 4 -> 2); test recall 25/27 -> 23/27, test precision 67.6% both (12 -> 11 trap hits). The dev trap-hit gap (4 -> 2) is two docs the control flagged in 1 of 3 repeats, neither targeted by this change (2026-22810, and 2026-21922 as a Brightside trap); the control's own dev trap hits on the old dev week were 2, 4 and 3 across three identical-config suites. Test gaps are inside the control's A/A swing.

iterations.title: Jev re-ranks passages inside its top 20 docs; the LLM filter reads the best ones, not just the abstract
iterations.decision: Promoted: jev-sonnet-strict-passages becomes the live setup (experiment.yaml userView.setup). Rule from the plan: promote if test recall and test trap hits are no worse than the control beyond the band. Pooled over suite 1 and the unchanged replicate (per 18 runs): test misses 5.3 (control) vs 3.1 (passages), test trap hits 10.6 vs 8.7; dev misses 3.0 vs 2.6, dev trap hits 3.5 vs 2.6. Both test metrics are better, but each overall gap is inside the control's A/A band (test misses swing 4.4, test trap hits 4.0 across its four identical-config suites), so the overall gain is not proven; the targeted gain is: 2026-21922 flagged 0/6 by the control in these suites (and in every earlier suite) vs 9/9 with passages, including the dev gate. Trade-off found: with passages the filter sometimes drops the DEA quota rules 2026-22842 and 2026-22843 (3 of 8 dev runs each; the control keeps them), likely because the passages state the duties fall on manufacturers. Cost per run $0.126 -> ~$0.20. Rule difference, stated openly: this plan's rule ("no worse beyond the band") is looser than the tie-breaker written in 05's notes ("inconclusive -> the cheaper setup stays", under which 04 was dropped on cost). It was written before this suite ran, so it stands; under 05's rule this would be inconclusive. Robustness: per suite, test misses were 4 vs 3 (l92) and 6 vs 3 (du8), test trap hits 11 vs 6 (l92) and 9 vs 9 (du8); on company-week x repeat slots where both setups finished (34 each): test misses 10 vs 6, trap hits 20 vs 15; dev misses 6 vs 5, trap hits 6 vs 5. On dev this is a trade (one doc fixed, two degraded), and flags-only 3-run agreement regressed from 89.5% to 82.5%.
